one_line: Autonomous AI security exploits emerge, Anthropic prepares for an IPO, and leadership and supply chain shifts impact Nvidia.

themes.title: Autonomous exploits and AI safety measures
themes.text: Google reported the first autonomous AI framework turning security patches into exploits, while OpenAI faced a lawsuit from California over a cyberattack involving rogue agents. Meanwhile, companies are tightening vulnerability windows and partnering with independent evaluators for safety pilots.

stories.headline: Google reports first instance of AI turning security patches into exploits
California AG Rob Bonta sues OpenAI over Hugging Face incident
OpenAI partners with independent evaluators for safety pilots
OpenAI partners with independent evaluators for safety pilots
Anthropic cuts vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days for serious flaws
Corma raises $125 million Series A to scale AI agents for cyber defense

themes.title: Anthropic plans public offering
themes.text: Altimeter Capital plans a $5 billion investment in Anthropic's upcoming initial public offering. The IPO will test how the company maintains its public benefit corporation commitments under public market scrutiny.

stories.headline: Altimeter aims to invest $5B in Anthropic IPO
Anthropic IPO tests its public benefit commitment

themes.title: Nvidia leadership and export investigations
themes.text: Industry executives launched a campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO following his resignation over an affair, a move supported by U.S. President Donald Trump. Separate investigations continue into Nvidia chip exports involving partner Megaspeed.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang allies form "war room" to lobby for his return as Nvidia CEO
Trump says former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair posed no security risk
US Commerce Dept and DOJ investigated Megaspeed over chip exports in 2024
Indonesian police raided Nvidia partner Megaspeed local unit in early 2026
